title: Disclosure schedules / MG6 / MG6C
purpose: Structural and realism reference for fictional test-document generation only.

structural_fields.name: schedule_version_or_date
structural_fields.notes: Submission date; later additional schedules continue numbering

structural_fields.name: description_of_item
structural_fields.notes: Meaningful description; not bare form numbers; avoid unexplained acronyms

structural_fields.name: sensitivity_reason
structural_fields.notes: MG6D only – reason for sensitivity belief

structural_fields.name: prosecutor_decision
structural_fields.notes: Disclose / inspect / not disclose; or agree sensitivity / PII needed

structural_fields.name: rebuttable_presumption_category
structural_fields.notes: AG Guidelines / CPIA Code categories where applicable

realistic_density_and_continuation.continuation_behaviour: Continuation sheets or later additional schedules; item numbers must remain consecutive to earlier schedules; additional MG6E accompanies later schedules.
realistic_density_and_continuation.whitespace_pattern: Dense tabular rows; description column widest; decisions column narrow.
realistic_density_and_continuation.overflow_rules: Long descriptions wrap within cell or spill to next row with same item number only if schedule convention allows; prefer complete row then next item.

tables_signatures_identifiers.tables: Core artefact is a numbered table: Item | Description | Location | (Sensitivity reason) | Prosecutor decision.
tables_signatures_identifiers.signatures: Disclosure officer signature/certification; prosecutor endorsements on decision columns.
tables_signatures_identifiers.identifiers: Item numbers unique and consecutive; cross-refs to exhibit marks / digital media IDs.
tables_signatures_identifiers.chequered_banding: Sensitive schedule (MG6D) is not disclosed to defence; chequered/non-disclosable marking common.

common_document_relationships.relation: Digital blocks/metadata often scheduled on MG6C with DMD strategy
Unused BWV/CCTV listed; rebuttable presumption categories apply
MG6D sensitivity may lead to CrimPR 15.3 PII application
Email corpuses block-listed with search-term methodology

safe_fictionalisation_rules: Use wholly invented names, addresses, DOBs, phone numbers, URN/PTI numbers, exhibit marks, and force identifiers.
Do not reproduce protected personal data from real cases, private case papers, or non-public force templates.
Prefer clearly fictional markers (e.g. 'FX-' URNs, 'Anytown', invented force codes) while preserving structural realism.
Do not copy Crown copyright form artwork/logos beyond structural field labels described in public guidance.
Where exact blank-form layout is unpublished, record layout confidence as inferred_from_guidance and avoid pixel-perfect claims.
Invent unused-item descriptions that are plausible but non-identifying.
Include some rebuttable-presumption class items (crime report, interview records, CCTV) with adequate descriptions.
For MG6D, invent sensitivity reasons at category level only (e.g. 'informant identity') without real operational detail.
visual_qa_requirements: Consecutive item numbering with no gaps after continuations.
Description column contains enough detail for a prosecutor decision (not 'CCTV' alone).
MG6C vs MG6D clearly labelled; sensitive reasons only on MG6D.
Prosecutor decision column present even if blank pending endorsement in fictional packs.
MG6E certification block present when pack claims disclosure officer report included.
prohibited_copying_or_unsupported_assump: No private case papers, custody-system screenshots, or force intranet templates.
No real victim/witness/defendant identifiers, phone numbers, IMEIs, vehicle registrations, or medical identifiers.
No reproduction of protected sensitive/PII schedules containing real sensitive material.
No claim that this register is a substitute for live CrimPR/Practice Direction forms.
No coupling to V2.1.2 renderer implementation; this pack is reference-only.
Do not copy real unused schedules from cases.
Do not place sensitive material descriptions on a defence-facing MG6C.
Do not assume GAP guilty-plea files always contain full MG6C (CPIA scheduling triggers differ).
